dev.update.already_running.note: Error shown in Settings > Device version when Update is pressed while the device is already updating itself.

dev.update.applying.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version while the device updates itself: it is applying the changes of one release. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.binary_install_failed.text: could not install the new binary
dev.update.binary_install_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device built its new program but could not put it in place; nothing was changed.

dev.update.build_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device builds its own program from source and that failed. {path} is the update log's path (also in Settings > Logs > Updates).

dev.update.building.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version while the device builds its new program from source (it takes a few minutes).

dev.update.checking.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version as an update starts: the device is reading the list of releases.

dev.update.checking_signature.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version as an update starts: the device checks that the list of releases is signed by the project.

dev.update.container_pull.text: This device runs in Docker and is updated with its image: on its server, run docker compose pull and then docker compose up -d.
dev.update.container_pull.note: Shown in Settings > Device version on a device that runs in Docker (a container on a home server or NAS), in place of the Update button, and as the reply to Update in an app that doesn't know about Docker yet. Such a device can't update itself: its owner pulls the new image on the server it runs on. docker compose pull and docker compose up -d are commands typed on that server: keep them exactly as they are.

dev.update.downloading.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version while the device downloads a release's source code. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.generating_protobuf.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version during a build step. protobuf is the name of the message format the apps and the device speak; keep it as it is.

dev.update.installing_web.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version while the device downloads the release's web app.

dev.update.interrupted.text: The update was interrupted - press Update to try again
dev.update.interrupted.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The update stopped before it finished (a power cut, a restart). Update is the name of the button that starts an update.

dev.update.manifest_download_failed.text: could not download the release manifest
dev.update.manifest_download_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The list of releases (the manifest) could not be downloaded.

dev.update.manifest_fetch_failed.text: could not fetch the release manifest
dev.update.manifest_fetch_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The list of releases (the manifest) could not be downloaded.

dev.update.manifest_not_signed.text: the release manifest is not signed with this project's release key - nothing was installed
dev.update.manifest_not_signed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The list of releases (the manifest) is not signed by the project, so the device refused it as possibly altered and installed nothing.

dev.update.no_release_key.text: this device has no release signing key ({path}) - reinstall or update by hand
dev.update.no_release_key.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device lacks the project's public key that checks releases, so it can't update itself. {path} is where that key should be, /etc/otc/release-signing.pub.

dev.update.no_room.text: no room to stage the update
dev.update.no_room.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device had no space to unpack the update.

dev.update.no_source_archive.text: release {release} has no signed source archive
dev.update.no_source_archive.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The signed list of releases names no source code for that release, so it can't be installed. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.no_source_dir.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The folder the source code is staged in is missing. {path} is that folder, /opt/otc-src.

dev.update.protobuf_version_missing.text: couldn't find google.golang.org/protobuf's version in go.mod
dev.update.protobuf_version_missing.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A build step could not find a library's version. google.golang.org/protobuf (a library) and go.mod (a file) are names: keep them as they are.

dev.update.protoc_download_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A build tool, protoc (its name), could not be downloaded. {version} is its version, such as 29.3.

dev.update.protoc_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A build tool, protoc (its name), failed.

dev.update.protoc_gen_go_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A build tool, protoc-gen-go (its name), could not be installed. {version} is its version, such as v1.36.6.

dev.update.protoc_hash_mismatch.text: protoc {version} does not match its pinned hash
dev.update.protoc_hash_mismatch.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A downloaded build tool, protoc (its name), is not the file it should be (its checksum differs), so it was refused. {version} is its version, such as 29.3.

dev.update.protoc_unpack_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A downloaded build tool, protoc (its name), could not be unpacked.

dev.update.repo_not_https.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device's configuration names a place to update from that isn't a secure (HTTPS) address, so the device refused it. {url} is that address.

dev.update.request_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Device version when Update was pressed but the device could not ask its root helper to start the update. {detail} is the system's own error, in English, such as permission denied.

dev.update.restarting.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version at the end of an update: the device installs its new program and restarts, which drops the connection for a moment.

dev.update.runner_chmod_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Device version when Update was pressed on a device set up by hand: the downloaded update script could not be made runnable. {detail} is the system's own error, in English.

dev.update.runner_download_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Device version when Update was pressed on a device set up by hand: the update script could not be downloaded. {detail} is the system's own error, in English.

dev.update.runner_start_failed.note: Error shown in Settings > Device version when Update was pressed on a device set up by hand: the update script could not be started. {detail} is the system's own error, in English.

dev.update.script_checksum.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A release's migration script is not the file the signed list of releases says (its checksum differs), so it was not run. {release} is the release's number; {expected} and {actual} are the two checksums (long hexadecimal strings).

dev.update.script_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A release's migration script (database or system changes) failed; the update can be tried again. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.script_missing.text: release {release}'s script is not in the verified source
dev.update.script_missing.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. A release's migration script is missing from the downloaded, checked source code. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.source_download_failed.text: could not download the source of release {release}
dev.update.source_download_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The release's source code could not be downloaded. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.source_hash_mismatch.text: the source of release {release} does not match its signed hash
dev.update.source_hash_mismatch.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The downloaded source code is not what the signed list of releases says (its checksum differs), so it was refused as possibly altered. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.source_unpack_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The release's downloaded source code could not be unpacked. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.stage_failed.text: could not stage the new source
dev.update.stage_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The new source code could not be copied into place for the build.

dev.update.staging.note: Progress line in Settings > Device version while the device copies the new release's source code into place for the build.

dev.update.unsupported_arch.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The device's processor type is not one the update can build for. {arch} is that type as the system names it, such as armv7l.

dev.update.updated.note: Shown in Settings > Device version once an update finished. {version} is the release number the device is now on, such as 118.

dev.update.uptodate.note: Shown in Settings > Device version when Update found nothing to install: the device already runs the newest release.

dev.update.verified_manifest_missing.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The checked list of releases (the manifest) that the update started from has disappeared.

dev.update.web_checksum.text: the web assets failed their checksum (expected {expected}, got {actual})
dev.update.web_checksum.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The downloaded web app is not the file the signed list of releases says (its checksum differs), so it was refused. {expected} and {actual} are the two checksums (long hexadecimal strings).

dev.update.web_download_failed.text: could not download the web app for release {release} - try the update again
dev.update.web_download_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The release's web app could not be downloaded; nothing was installed and pressing Update again retries. {release} is the release's number, such as 118.

dev.update.web_install_failed.text: could not install the web assets
dev.update.web_install_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The new web app could not be put in place.

dev.update.web_unpack_failed.text: could not unpack the web assets
dev.update.web_unpack_failed.note: Why an update failed, after Update failed: in Settings > Device version. The downloaded web app could not be unpacked.
